```python
def fit_genotype(g):
    design = make_design(Theta, tr, g)
    return fit_stlsq(design.Theta, design.dy)

coefs = pd.DataFrame({g: fit_genotype(g) for g in tr.genotypes},
                     index=["1"] + Theta.terms)
print(coefs["g114"].round(4))
```

```{r}

#| echo: false
fit_genotype <- function(g) {
  design <- make_design(Theta, tr, g)
  fit_stlsq(design$Theta, design$dy)
}
coefs <- sapply(tr$genotypes, fit_genotype)
round(coefs[, "g114"], 4)
```

Terms with a coefficient of zero were removed. Written out for `g114`, with the standardised drivers,

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
cat(equation_latex(coefs[, "g114"]))
```

Individual coefficients of a polynomial are difficult to interpret, so the equation is examined through the growth rate it implies.

```python
for year, colour in zip([1984, 1998, 2008], [BLUE, CYAN, BURGUNDY]):
    ax.plot(das, rate[list(tr.years).index(year)], color=colour, lw=1.2,

ax.legend(frameon=False)
```

```{r}
#| label: 06-2-run

n_days <- dim(Theta)[2]
rate_y <- function(y) cbind(1, Theta[y, , ]) %*% coefs[, "g114"]
rates <- data.frame(das = rep(1:n_days + tr$das0 - 1, length(tr$years)),
                    year = rep(tr$years, each = n_days),
                    rate = unlist(lapply(seq_along(tr$years), rate_y)))
rates <- rates[rates$das <= tr$das0 + max(tr$nend) - 1, ]
shown <- rates[rates$year %in% c(1984, 1998, 2008), ]

ggplot(rates, aes(das, rate, group = year)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#D1D5DB", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(data = shown, aes(colour = factor(year)), linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_dgxe("blue", "cyan", "burgundy") +
  labs(x = "days after sowing", y = "growth rate (t/ha/day)") +
  theme_dgxe() +
  legend_top()
```

For this additive library the rate is a sum of one function per driver, so its contributions can be separated. For year 1998:

## Python

```python
PALETTE = ["#014E81", "#00A6D6", "#8B1E3F", "#469C2A", "#6F1D77", "#EF60A3", "#00A390", "#9CA3AF", "#1F2937"]
s = list(tr.years).index(1998)
n = tr.nend[np.searchsorted(tr.genotypes, "g114"), s] + 1
parts = {}
for name in drv.drivers:
    cols = [i for i, t in enumerate(Theta.terms) if t.startswith(name)]
    parts[name] = Theta.array[s, :n][:, cols] @ b[1 + np.array(cols)]
parts["total"] = b[0] + sum(parts.values())
das = np.arange(n) + tr.das0

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 2.8))
ax.axhline(0, color="#9CA3AF", lw=0.5)
for (name, y), colour in zip(parts.items(), PALETTE):
    ax.plot(das, y, color=colour, lw=2 if name == "total" else 1, label=name)
ax.legend(frameon=False, ncol=5, fontsize=7)
ax.set_xlabel("days after sowing")
ax.set_ylabel("contribution to growth rate (t/ha/day)")
fig.tight_layout()
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: 06-3-run
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 2.8
contribution <- function(driver) {
  terms <- grep(paste0("^", driver), dimnames(Theta)[[3]])
  Theta[match(1998, tr$years), , terms] %*% coefs[1 + terms, "g114"]
}
palette <- c("#014E81", "#00A6D6", "#8B1E3F", "#469C2A", "#6F1D77", "#EF60A3", "#00A390", "#9CA3AF", "#1F2937")
parts <- sapply(drv$drivers, contribution)
contributions <- data.frame(
  das = rep(1:n_days + tr$das0 - 1, ncol(parts) + 1),
  part = factor(rep(c(drv$drivers, "total"), each = n_days),
                c(drv$drivers, "total")),
  value = c(parts, coefs[1, "g114"] + rowSums(parts)))
contributions <- contributions[
  contributions$das <= tr$das0 + tr$nend["g114", match(1998, tr$years)], ]

ggplot(contributions, aes(das, value, colour = part, linewidth = part)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#9CA3AF", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = palette) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(rep(0.6, ncol(parts)), 1.1)) +
  labs(x = "days after sowing", y = "contribution to growth rate (t/ha/day)") +
  theme_dgxe() +
  legend_top()
```

The growth rate (total) is the sum of the eight contributions and the constant term (not shown).

The same decomposition for any genotype and year:

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
d3 = window.d3
Plot = window.Plot
contrib = FileAttachment("data/interactive/contrib.json").json()
viewof genotype2 = select("Genotype", contrib.genotypes, "g114")
viewof year2 = slider("Year", contrib.years, contrib.years.indexOf(1998))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const g = contrib.genotypes.indexOf(genotype2);
  const b = contrib.coefs[g];
  const days = contrib.nend[g][year2] + 1;
  const theta = contrib.theta[year2].slice(0, days);
  const parts = contrib.drivers.map(name => {
    const cols = contrib.terms.map((t, j) => t.startsWith(name) ? j : -1).filter(j => j >= 0);
    return theta.map((row, i) => ({
      das: contrib.das0 + i, part: name,
      value: d3.sum(cols, j => b[1 + j] * row[j])}));
  });
  const total = theta.map((row, i) => ({das: contrib.das0 + i, part: "total",
    value: b[0] + d3.sum(parts, p => p[i].value)}));
  const colours = ["#014E81", "#00A6D6", "#8B1E3F", "#469C2A", "#6F1D77", "#EF60A3", "#00A390", "#9CA3AF", "#1F2937"];
  return Plot.plot({
    width: 640, height: 320, marginLeft: 55,
    x: {label: "days after sowing"},
    y: {label: "contribution to growth rate (t/ha/day)"},
    color: {domain: [...contrib.drivers, "total"], range: colours, legend: true},
    marks: [Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: "#9CA3AF"}),
            Plot.line([...parts.flat(), ...total], {x: "das", y: "value", stroke: "part",
              strokeWidth: d => d.part === "total" ? 2.5 : 1.3})]
  });
}
```


## Effect of a single driver

The effect of one driver cannot be read by varying it alone while the others are held fixed, since the drivers are correlated in real weather:

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
#| label: 06-4
#| ref.label: 06-4-run
#| eval: false
```

## Python

```python
Z = observed_points(drv, tr)
print(Z.corr().round(2))
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: 06-4-run
#| echo: false
Z <- as.data.frame(observed_points(drv, tr))
round(cor(Z), 2)
```

Accumulated local effects (ALE) vary the driver only within narrow intervals around values that occur, using the observed values of the other drivers, and accumulate the resulting changes in the growth rate. For the fitted growth rate $f(\mathbf{u}) = \boldsymbol{\theta}(\mathbf{u})^\top \hat{\boldsymbol{\xi}}$ and driver $j$,

$$
\mathrm{ALE}_j(z) = \int_{z_0}^{z} \mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{\partial f(\mathbf{u})}{\partial u_j} \,\middle|\, u_j = v\right] dv - c,
$$

where $z_0$ is the smallest observed value and the constant $c$ centres the curve at mean zero over the data. The expectation is estimated over the observations in each interval of a grid (24 intervals here). The `iml` package computes ALE curves for any model that provides a prediction function; here the model is the growth rate of a genotype.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
#| label: 06-5
#| ref.label: [06-5-run, 06-5-show]
#| eval: false
```

## Python

```python
import logging

from PyALE import ale

logging.getLogger().setLevel(logging.WARNING)

def natural(z, j):
    return z * drv.scale[j] + drv.center[j]

def ale_genotype(g, j):
    rate = GrowthRate(coefs[g].to_numpy())
    effect = ale(Z, rate, [drv.drivers[j]], grid_size=24,
                 include_CI=False, plot=False)
    return pd.DataFrame({"genotype": g, "driver": drv.drivers[j],
                         "x": natural(effect.index.to_numpy(), j),
                         "effect": effect["eff"].to_numpy()})

curves = pd.concat(ale_genotype(g, j)
                   for g in tr.genotypes for j in range(len(drv.drivers)))
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: 06-5-run
#| echo: false
predictor <- function(coef, pairs = FALSE) {
  rate <- function(model, newdata) {
    L <- library_matrix(as.matrix(newdata), pairs = pairs)
    as.vector(cbind(1, L) %*% model)
  }
  Predictor$new(coef, data = Z, predict.function = rate)
}

natural <- function(z, j) z * drv$scale[j] + drv$center[j]
ale_genotype <- function(g, j) {
  effect <- FeatureEffect$new(predictor(coefs[, g]), drv$drivers[j],
                              method = "ale", grid.size = 24)$results
  data.frame(genotype = g, driver = factor(drv$drivers[j], drv$drivers),
             x = natural(effect[[drv$drivers[j]]], j), effect = effect$.value)
}
cells <- expand.grid(g = tr$genotypes, j = seq_along(drv$drivers),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: 06-5-show
#| eval: false
#| include: false
curves <- do.call(rbind, Map(ale_genotype, cells$g, cells$j))
```

```{r}

```

```{r}
}))

ggplot(curves, aes(x, effect, group = genotype)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#9CA3AF", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(colour = "#D1D5DB", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_line(data = curves[curves$genotype %in% highlighted, ],
            aes(colour = genotype), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_rug(data = observed, aes(x = x), inherit.aes = FALSE, sides = "b",
           alpha = 0.03) +
  facet_wrap(~driver, ncol = 2, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_dgxe("burgundy", "cyan", "blue") +
  labs(x = "driver value (original units)",
       y = "effect on growth rate (t/ha/day)") +
  theme_dgxe() +
  legend_top()
```

The rug marks show where data exist. Thermal time is accumulated from sowing, so its curve describes the dependence of growth on the stage of the year, not a response to temperature. Thermal time and day length are correlated at 0.97 and are best read together.

## Interactions and partial dependence

The library of powers is additive in the drivers: the effect of one driver does not depend on the others, and ALE and partial dependence coincide. With products of pairs of drivers (108 terms, backward elimination to 20 terms) they differ. For `g114`, partial dependence averages the growth rate over all observed days while one driver is set to each value in turn.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
#| label: 06-7
#| ref.label: 06-7-run
#| eval: false
```

## Python

```python
Theta2 = make_library(drv, pairs=True)
design2 = make_design(Theta2, tr, "g114")
rate2 = GrowthRate(fit_subset(design2.Theta, design2.dy, k=20, method="backward"), pairs=True)

def effects(feature):
    j = drv.drivers.index(feature)
    a = ale(Z, rate2, [feature], grid_size=24, include_CI=False, plot=False)
    grid = np.linspace(Z[feature].min(), Z[feature].max(), 24)
    pdp = np.array([rate2.predict(Z.assign(**{feature: v})).mean()
                    for v in grid])
    return (natural(grid, j), pdp - pdp.mean(),
            natural(a.index.to_numpy(), j), a["eff"].to_numpy())
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: 06-7-run
#| echo: false
Theta2 <- make_library(drv, pairs = TRUE)
design2 <- make_design(Theta2, tr, "g114")
pred2 <- predictor(fit_subset(design2$Theta, design2$dy, k = 20, method = "backward"), TRUE)

effects <- function(j) {
  feature <- drv$drivers[j]
  ale <- FeatureEffect$new(pred2, feature, "ale", grid.size = 24)$results
  pdp <- FeatureEffect$new(pred2, feature, "pdp", grid.size = 24)$results
  pdp$x <- natural(pdp[[feature]], j)
  pdp$driver <- factor(feature, drv$drivers)
  pdp$.value <- pdp$.value - mean(pdp$.value)
  ale$x <- natural(ale[[feature]], j)
  ale$driver <- pdp$driver[1]
  pdp[[feature]] <- NULL
  ale[[feature]] <- NULL
  list(pdp = pdp, ale = ale)
}
parts <- lapply(1:2, effects)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

```python
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 3))
for ax, feature in zip(axes, ["TT", "DL"]):
    x, pdp, xa, a = effects(feature)
    ax.plot(x, pdp, color=BURGUNDY, lw=1.5, label="partial dependence")
    ax.plot(xa, a, "--", color=BLUE, lw=1.5, label="ALE")
    ax.set_title(feature, loc="left")
axes[0].legend(frameon=False)
fig.supxlabel("driver value")
fig.supylabel("effect on growth rate (t/ha/day)")
fig.tight_layout()
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: 06-8-run
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 3
bind <- function(name) do.call(rbind, lapply(parts, `[[`, name))
pdp <- bind("pdp"); ale <- bind("ale")

ggplot(pdp, aes(x, .value)) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = "partial dependence"), linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_line(data = ale, aes(y = .value, colour = "ALE"), linewidth = 0.9,
            linetype = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~driver, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_dgxe("blue", "burgundy") +
  labs(x = "driver value", y = "effect on growth rate (t/ha/day)") +
  theme_dgxe() +
  legend_top()
```

The two curves differ because of the interactions. Partial dependence also evaluates the model at combinations of drivers that do not occur in the data, for example a short day late in a year with high thermal time, whereas ALE does not.
